item.title: 5 Storylines to Watch as NASCAR Opens at Daytona
item.description: From Connor Zilisch’s debut to playoff changes and redemption bids, the 2026 season begins with plenty at stake.

item.title: Ford’s EV Plan Is Unchanged from a Year Ago
item.description: All-new UEV platform on track for 2027; Ford expects $1 billion tariff hit in 2026.

item.title: Keselowski Says Return From Broken Femur Is Still a Question
item.description: “Worst pain I ever went through”: RFK Racing co-owner admits Daytona will be his first true test after a painful skiing injury.

item.title: SVG Enters Daytona Hoping Oval Gains Continue
item.description: After a dominant rookie year on road courses, improvement on ovals is the next step.

item.title: How McLaren Plans to Remain atop F1’s Summit
item.description: After sweeping both the Drivers’ and Constructors’ F1 titles in 2025, McLaren believes starting from zero is the key to defending them.

item.title: Lamborghini Goes North, Far North, with Esperienza Neve
item.description: Lambos on ice turns out to be nice!

item.title: Larson Locks In Long-Term Deal with Hendrick Ahead of Daytona
item.description: The defending Cup champion signs a five-year extension before qualifying for the 500.

item.title: EPA Moves to Eliminate Incentives for Auto Start/Stop Systems
item.description: The Trump administration says the fuel-saving feature is unpopular and plans to end regulatory credits that encouraged its use.

item.title: How the Daytona 500 Stopped Being About Raw Speed
item.description: Nearly 70 years after its debut, NASCAR’s biggest race is decided less by horsepower and more by survival.

item.title: Travis Pastrana Back Behind the Wheel for Daytona Trucks
item.description: The stunt legend calls NASCAR “chess at 200 miles per hour,” says stock car racing is “way more stressful than you imagine.”
